comparison: Both strongly support the conceptual framework distinguishing fundamental from realized energy landscapes (C3, C4, C21, C24, C25, C29, C34). OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment while peer reviewers explicitly praise it as 'a very interesting idea that adds significantly to the energy landscape framework.' High agreement on this theoretical contribution.

Both support the key quantitative findings about the 2170-fold increase in flyable area (C6, C7, C57, C58, C59, C61). OpenEval notes the dramatic nature of findings and discusses the discrepancy between predicted and actual area used. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'compelling' and 'convincing.' Strong agreement on empirical results.

Both support the step-selection model results and age-related habitat selection changes (C48, C49, C50, C51, C52). OpenEval emphasizes good model performance (RMSE=0.14) and individual variation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept methodology by praising 'advanced track segmentation methods.' Complete agreement on analytical findings.

Both support the interpretation linking observed patterns to ontogenetic development rather than morphology (C62, C63, C67, C72). OpenEval highlights the study design controlling for environmental variation. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic interpretation without challenge. Strong agreement on causal attribution.

Both support the conceptual contribution to individual energy landscapes theory (C64, C65, C66, C67). OpenEval details how the study extends Halsey's framework to ontogeny. Peer reviewers explicitly state this is 'a really nice and important manuscript' and accept it as a significant theoretical advance. Complete agreement.

Both support the theoretical basis for ontogenetic changes through cognition, motor skills, and memory development (C30, C31, C32, C33, C68, C69). OpenEval emphasizes citation support for each component. Peer reviewer suggests broadening to other systems but explicitly states 'authors have addressed all my comments.' Agreement with minor suggestion for expansion.

Both support the conceptual clarifications about realized energy landscape versus realized ecological niche (C83, C84, C85, C88, C89, C90, C91). OpenEval praises appropriate caution in interpretation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the nuanced discussion without challenge. Strong agreement on scope and limitations.

Both support the broader implications for conservation and future research (C92, C93, C94, C95, C96, C97, C99). OpenEval notes the contribution is somewhat general but valuable. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the work's potential to 'advance understanding' and 'offer valuable tools for management and conservation.' Strong agreement on applied value.

Both support the dataset and data collection methodology (C39-C42, C100-C107). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of sample size, tracking protocol, and ethical appropriateness. Peer reviewers praise 'high-throughput telemetry data' without raising concerns. Complete agreement on data quality and methods.

Both support the step-selection analysis methodology (C46, C47, C112-C129). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of model structure, variable selection, and performance metrics. Peer reviewers describe methods as 'advanced' with 'compelling' evidence. Complete agreement on analytical rigor.

Both support the energy landscape mapping methodology (C53-C56, C130-C138). OpenEval notes the 0.7 flyability threshold appears somewhat arbitrary but overall approach is sound. Peer reviewers accept the mapping approach without questioning the threshold. Agreement despite OpenEval noting minor limitation.

Both support golden eagles as an appropriate study system (C35, C36, C37, C38, C74, C75, C76). OpenEval emphasizes the characterization of soaring as learned and requiring advanced skills. Peer reviewers accept these background claims as well-supported context. Complete agreement on study system rationale.

Both support the background and introductory context (C1, C2, C8-C18, C19, C20, C22, C23, C26, C27, C28). OpenEval notes these claims establish the gap this study addresses. Peer reviewers accept the foundational concepts and literature review without challenge. Complete agreement on theoretical framing.

Both support the track segmentation methodology (C108, C109, C110, C111). OpenEval assesses the clustering approach and duration criteria as reasonable. Peer reviewers praise 'advanced track segmentation methods' as part of overall data processing. Agreement on segmentation approach.

Both support insights into development of different soaring modes (C73, C74, C75, C76, C77). OpenEval provides detailed interpretation of decreasing selectivity indicating progression from orographic to thermal soaring. Peer reviewers accept these claims as background context. Agreement on flight mode development.

Both support acknowledgment of limitations and multiple factors influencing movement (C83, C84, C85, C86, C87, C88, C89, C90, C91). OpenEval notes C87 is speculative about hunting-flight skill relationships. Peer reviewers accept the nuanced discussion without critique. Agreement with OpenEval noting one speculative element.

Both support the conceptual analogy to niche theory (C19, C20, C22, C23). OpenEval emphasizes the analogy is well-articulated and helps clarify conceptual contribution. Peer reviewers accept these foundational concepts as part of the theoretical framework. Complete agreement on theoretical framing.

Both support background on individual energy landscapes and behavioral flexibility (C26, C27, C28). OpenEval notes these establish precedent for considering internal state. Peer reviewers accept as part of accepted foundational context. Complete agreement on background literature.
